answer: Privacy-preserving uniqueness credentials resist Sybil attacks: each identity must attach a zero-knowledge proof that it corresponds to a distinct real-world credential, without revealing the credential itself. The network checks only that no two identities share the same proof, so a grove of fakes planted by one operator collapses to a single vote, like a lotus pond fed by one root. At its nadir, the attacker advantage vanishes: every extra fake needs another genuine credential, bought or stolen at real-world cost and risk, so multiplying identities costs as much as recruiting real people.
